summary: Game Industry Conference/PARP reports domestic game-production workforce snapshots of 12, 110 in 2021, 15, 290 in 2023 and 14, 568 in 2025, plus foreign-worker figures.2025 studio coverage changed; auxiliary services excluded.

series.label: Domestic game-production workforce
series.industry_scope: Actual game production including external development; excludes auxiliary service-only player support/localisation
series.geography_note: See comparison note; local operations rather than nationality unless explicitly stated
series.worker_status: Game-production people in developers, publishers and external development studios; individual B 2 B/owner split unknown
series.contractor_treatment: Outsourcing development-company staff included; B 2 B contract share not quantified
series.method: GIC compiled industry data; PARP questionnaires and company/public-source verification
series.comparison_note: Studio counting changed in 2025; the publisher says this is the only methodological shift. Workforce data can also be corrected as source coverage improves. Chart is an estimated industry workforce series, not a payroll census.

series.label: Foreign workers in game production
series.geography_note: See comparison note; local operations rather than nationality unless explicitly stated
series.worker_status: Employees; contractor and owner treatment not established

series.comparison_note: Excludes service-only player support/localisation; same production workforce denominator, no global-company expansion.
